purpose: Plan, evaluate, and execute metadata and resource description work units (type modeling, schema selection, descriptive/administrative/structural/preservation encoding, conceptual/content models, application profiles, controlled vocabularies, persistent identifiers, linked-data expression, crosswalks, harvesting, and quality) as a subdomain node of a knowledge-searcher meta-KB.
assumptions: subdomain of information science and knowledge organization; framed for a knowledge-searcher meta-KB
no observed dataset supplied; all numeric values are heuristic priors
covers metadata schemas, conceptual/content models, profiles, quality, linked data, identifiers, and interoperability
session-bounded work units suitable for heavy LLM-assisted execution and handoff
exclusions: full-text indexing and ranking (information retrieval subdomain)
classification scheme and taxonomy authoring (knowledge organization systems subdomain)
repository software engineering and storage infrastructure
rights/licensing legal adjudication beyond rights-metadata capture

competency_questions.question: What metadata functions (descriptive, administrative, structural, preservation) must this resource set capture?
Which schema(s) fit the resource type, community, and granularity needs?
When should Dublin Core vs MODS vs MARC21 vs EAD be used for description?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: descriptive schema nodes present with scope and DC-vs-MODS conflict axis

competency_questions.question: How are descriptive, administrative, and structural metadata bound into one complex object?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: METS present depending on MODS and PREMIS

competency_questions.question: What preservation metadata is needed to trust objects over the long term?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PREMIS present with fixity/event acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: Which conceptual/content model (FRBR/IFLA LRM, RDA, BIBFRAME) grounds the description semantics?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONCEPTUAL_MODEL, RDA_CONTENT, BIBFRAME present with dependency edges

competency_questions.question: How are usage rules, cardinality, and controlled values fixed for a community?
How is metadata expressed as linked data / RDF using shared vocabularies and identifiers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: RDF_EXPRESSION present depending on profile, vocab, and identifiers

competency_questions.question: Which persistent identifier schemes are assigned to resources and agents, and how are they governed?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PERSISTENT_ID present with resolution acceptance tests

competency_questions.question: How are records mapped between schemas and aggregated/harvested across repositories?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CROSSWALK and HARVEST_AGGREGATE present with dependency edges

competency_questions.question: How is metadata quality measured and remediated?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_ASSESS and QUALITY_REMEDIATION present with assess->remediate dependency

competency_questions.question: Which quality dimensions (completeness, accuracy, conformance, consistency) apply and how are they reported?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: QUALITY_ASSESS scope includes named quality dimensions

competency_questions.question: How are profiles, vocabularies, and identifiers governed and versioned over the lifecycle?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: GOVERNANCE present with versioning scope and change_control

competency_questions.question: What ordering reduces rework when standing up metadata for a collection?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: workflow and priority_order place scope/model before encoding and quality

glossary.definition: metadata supporting discovery and identification of a resource
metadata for managing a resource (rights, technical, provenance)
metadata expressing how parts of a complex object relate and order
metadata supporting long-term retention, fixity, and provenance
a specification mixing elements from multiple schemas with usage rules
a mapping of elements/values between two metadata schemas
FRBR/LRM entities Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item
process binding access points to authorized, controlled forms
a durable, resolvable identifier for a resource or agent
data published as RDF with resolvable URIs enabling graph integration
protocol for harvesting metadata records from repositories
fitness for use across completeness, accuracy, conformance, consistency

evidence_label_policy.note: No observed/experimental inputs supplied; only heuristic labels are eligible.

source_registry.description: Heuristic priors from established metadata and resource-description literature (Joudrey & Taylor; Chan & Salaba; Svenonius) and library/archives practice; no measured dataset supplied.
grounding_limits: all numeric values are heuristic priors, not measurements
no observed or experimentally_validated labels are eligible

normalization_definitions.rounding: round computed scores to 2 decimals; tolerance 0.02

nodes.definition: Classify and scope the metadata to capture across descriptive, administrative, structural, and preservation functions before selecting any schema.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when new use cases (rights management, long-term preservation) expand required metadata functions

pros.claim: separating functions prevents conflating discovery fields with preservation fields
pros.example: keeping PREMIS event data out of a Dublin Core discovery record

cons.claim: over-segmentation can fragment a single logical resource description
cons.example: splitting one object across four schemas with no binding model

acceptance_tests: every required function maps to at least one planned element set
no function left uncovered for in-scope resource classes

nodes.definition: Choose the metadata schema(s) (Dublin Core, MODS, MARC21, EAD, etc.) that fit resource type, community, granularity, and interoperability needs.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when target community or aggregator changes required interoperability profile

pros.claim: matching schema to community maximizes downstream reuse and exchange
pros.example: choosing MODS for digital library objects needing richer bibliographic detail than DC

cons.claim: premature schema lock forces costly migration if requirements shift
cons.example: committing to MARC21 then needing linked-data expression

failure_modes: schema too coarse for required granularity
schema not supported by target aggregator
acceptance_tests: selected schema supports every required element in the function map
schema is recognized by target exchange partners

nodes.definition: Apply the Dublin Core element set (simple/qualified, DCMI Metadata Terms) for lightweight, cross-domain descriptive interoperability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when richer descriptive granularity is required beyond the 15 core elements

pros.claim: lowest-common-denominator interoperability across heterogeneous repositories
pros.example: OAI-PMH mandates oai_dc as the baseline metadata format

cons.claim: flatness causes semantic loss when crosswalked from richer schemas
cons.example: MARC subfields collapse into a single dc:title

acceptance_tests: all 15 elements validate against DCMI Terms
oai_dc export parses for harvesting

nodes.definition: Use the MODS XML schema for rich, MARC-compatible bibliographic description in digital library and repository contexts.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when records must round-trip to/from MARC21 with minimal loss

pros.claim: richer than DC yet more web-friendly than MARC, ideal for repositories
pros.example: embedding MODS in METS dmdSec for a digitized book

cons.claim: verbose XML increases authoring and validation cost
cons.example: deep nesting of name/role/affiliation subelements

acceptance_tests: MODS instance validates against the official schema
MARC->MODS->MARC round-trip preserves core fields

nodes.definition: Encode and maintain bibliographic and authority data in MARC21 fields, indicators, and subfields for legacy ILS interoperability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when migration toward BIBFRAME/linked data is planned

pros.claim: universal support across integrated library systems
pros.example: copy cataloging via Z39.50/MARC record exchange

cons.claim: flat record model resists linked-data expression and entity relationships
cons.example: author-as-string instead of a linkable authority entity

acceptance_tests: record validates against MARC21 format
indicators and mandatory fields present

nodes.definition: Describe archival materials hierarchically with Encoded Archival Description (finding aids) reflecting provenance and original order.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when archival description must aggregate into a portal requiring different granularity

pros.claim: preserves provenance and hierarchical context unique to archives
pros.example: one finding aid covering series, subseries, and folders

cons.claim: hierarchy flattens poorly into item-centric discovery systems
cons.example: a folder-level component losing context when harvested as a flat DC record

acceptance_tests: finding aid validates against EAD3 schema
hierarchy renders with inherited context

nodes.definition: Bind descriptive, administrative, and structural metadata plus file inventory into a METS wrapper expressing a complex digital object's structure.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when object complexity (multi-file, multi-page, derivatives) changes the required structural model

pros.claim: single container expresses page order, derivatives, and metadata binding
pros.example: a digitized newspaper issue with page-image structMap and per-file admin metadata

cons.claim: complex wrapper is brittle and tightly couples otherwise independent metadata
cons.example: a schema change in an embedded dmdSec invalidating the whole METS package

failure_modes: structMap does not match file inventory
acceptance_tests: METS validates against schema with all referenced files present
structMap fully covers fileSec entries

nodes.definition: Record preservation metadata (objects, events, agents, rights) using PREMIS to support long-term digital preservation and auditability.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when preservation policy, fixity cadence, or rights regime changes

pros.claim: captures the provenance and fixity needed to trust objects over decades
pros.example: logging a format migration event with agent and outcome

cons.claim: event verbosity grows unbounded without retention policy
cons.example: every fixity check appended as a full event indefinitely

acceptance_tests: every object has a fixity value and at least one provenance event
rights statements present for all preserved objects
PREMIS instance validates

nodes.definition: Model bibliographic entities and relationships (Work, Expression, Manifestation, Item; agents; subjects) using FRBR/IFLA LRM to ground description semantics.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when IFLA LRM revisions or RDA alignment change entity definitions

pros.claim: entity model enables collocation and FRBRization across formats
pros.example: grouping all expressions of one work under a single intellectual entity

cons.claim: abstract entities are hard to derive reliably from flat legacy records
cons.example: inferring Work identity from inconsistent MARC uniform titles

acceptance_tests: entity model maps consistently to chosen schemas
WEMI levels distinguishable in test records

nodes.definition: Apply RDA content/cataloging rules to determine how resource attributes and relationships are transcribed and recorded, independent of encoding schema.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when RDA Toolkit revisions or community profiles change recording rules

pros.claim: separates content rules from encoding, enabling reuse across schemas
pros.example: one RDA description rendered as MARC and as BIBFRAME

cons.claim: rule optionality causes inconsistency without a local policy
cons.example: varying transcription of statements of responsibility across catalogers

acceptance_tests: values conform to RDA element definitions
relationship designators used per policy

nodes.definition: Model bibliographic data as linked-data entities (Work, Instance, Item) in BIBFRAME to enable web-scale, RDF-based description and relationships.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when BIBFRAME vocabulary versions or conversion specs change

pros.claim: exposes bibliographic data to the semantic web and entity reuse
pros.example: linking a Work to external authority and subject URIs

cons.claim: MARC-to-BIBFRAME conversion is lossy and immature in tooling
cons.example: complex MARC relationships not surviving automated conversion

failure_modes: entity identity errors create duplicate Works
acceptance_tests: converted graph validates against BIBFRAME vocabulary
entities resolve to stable URIs

nodes.definition: Author an application profile (DCAP/DCTAP) that mixes elements from multiple namespaces with usage rules, cardinality, and value constraints for a community.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when community needs or referenced namespaces change element usage

pros.claim: profiles make interoperability concrete and testable for a community
pros.example: mandating dcterms:created with ISO 8601 cardinality 1..1

cons.claim: profiles drift from referenced standards without governance
cons.example: local refinements diverging from updated DCMI Terms

acceptance_tests: every profile element resolves to a defined namespace term
constraints expressible as SHACL/ShEx shapes

nodes.definition: Bind descriptive values to controlled vocabularies and authority files (LCSH, LCNAF, AAT, etc.) to ensure consistent, linkable access points.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when vocabularies are updated, deprecated, or merged upstream

pros.claim: controlled values enable collocation and linked-data reconciliation
pros.example: mapping a subject string to its LCSH URI for cross-system linking

cons.claim: vocabulary maintenance burden and version skew across systems
cons.example: a deprecated LCSH heading still present in legacy records

acceptance_tests: each controlled element resolves to a current authority/URI
no orphan headings outside the vocabulary

nodes.definition: Mint, assign, and govern persistent identifiers (DOI, Handle, ARK, ORCID, ISNI) so resources and agents remain citable and resolvable over time.

included: identifier schemes (DOI, Handle, ARK, ORCID, ISNI)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when resolution infrastructure, provider, or identifier policy changes

pros.claim: persistent, resolvable identifiers underpin citation and linked data
pros.example: a DOI resolving to current metadata after a URL change

cons.claim: once published, identifiers cannot be reassigned without breaking links
cons.example: a DOI minted for the wrong manifestation cannot be silently reused

acceptance_tests: every published identifier resolves to correct current metadata
no identifier collision across the namespace

nodes.definition: Express metadata as RDF triples using appropriate vocabularies and serializations to enable linked-data publishing and graph integration.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when target vocabularies, serialization, or graph store change

pros.claim: RDF enables merging metadata across sources via shared URIs
pros.example: joining a local graph with an external authority via owl:sameAs

cons.claim: poor vocabulary choices create non-interoperable triples
cons.example: inventing local predicates instead of reusing dcterms

acceptance_tests: serialized RDF parses and validates against chosen vocabularies
subjects use resolvable URIs

nodes.definition: Design and validate crosswalks that map elements and values between schemas (e.g., MARC<->MODS<->DC) while controlling semantic loss.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when a source or target schema version changes element semantics

pros.claim: crosswalks enable aggregation across heterogeneous repositories
pros.example: mapping MODS to oai_dc for a union catalog

cons.claim: every mapping risks semantic loss or false equivalence
cons.example: mapping MARC 700 relator codes to a single dc:contributor

acceptance_tests: round-trip preserves mandatory elements within tolerance
every source element maps or is explicitly dropped with rationale

nodes.definition: Expose and aggregate metadata via OAI-PMH (and related protocols) so records can be harvested, normalized, and combined across repositories.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when aggregator requirements or harvest formats change

pros.claim: standard harvesting enables portals and union catalogs at low cost
pros.example: a national portal harvesting oai_dc from hundreds of repositories

cons.claim: lowest-common-denominator harvest formats lose richness
cons.example: only oai_dc exposed, hiding richer MODS detail

acceptance_tests: harvest returns complete, valid records for requested sets
deleted/updated records reflected in incremental harvest

nodes.definition: Measure metadata against completeness, accuracy, conformance, consistency, and timeliness dimensions to quantify and report fitness for use.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when profile/constraints change or a new defect class is discovered

pros.claim: quantified quality guides remediation and exposes systemic defects
pros.example: reporting 30% of records missing a required date element

cons.claim: accuracy and relevance are hard to measure automatically
cons.example: a syntactically valid but factually wrong subject heading passes conformance

failure_modes: metrics not tied to fitness for use
acceptance_tests: each quality dimension has a defined, repeatable metric
conformance checked against the active application profile

nodes.definition: Plan and execute correction and enrichment of deficient metadata (batch fixes, enrichment, normalization) with controlled, auditable changes.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when re-measurement shows remediation did not improve targeted dimensions

pros.claim: systematic remediation lifts aggregate quality cost-effectively
pros.example: a global find-replace normalizing date formats to ISO 8601

cons.claim: unverified batch edits can introduce new, wider errors
cons.example: a regex normalization corrupting valid edge-case dates

acceptance_tests: post-remediation re-measurement shows targeted dimension improved
all changes captured in an auditable log

nodes.definition: Establish governance: roles, policies, versioning, and lifecycle controls so metadata standards and records remain consistent and maintainable over time.

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: when org structure, mandates, or referenced standards change

pros.claim: governance prevents profile/vocabulary drift and orphaned decisions
pros.example: a documented review cycle catching a deprecated namespace before it spreads

cons.claim: heavy governance can slow responsiveness to new requirements
cons.example: a multi-month approval delaying an urgent profile fix

acceptance_tests: every active profile and vocabulary has an owner and version
change-control records exist for locked artifacts

edges.why_related: function map defines what schema selection must cover
edges.example: function map missing preservation forces re-pick

edges.why_related: preservation function in the type model scopes PREMIS use
edges.example: no preservation function planned then PREMIS retrofit

edges.why_related: type scope informs which entities the conceptual model must cover
edges.risk_of_conflict: modeling entities not in scope wastes effort
edges.example: modeling agents not needed for the collection

edges.why_related: administrative function scopes identifier needs
edges.benefit_of_coupling: right identifiers for the right entities

edges.why_related: selection of DC governs whether DC records are produced
selection of MODS governs MODS authoring
edges.example: MODS chosen for archives over EAD

edges.why_related: selection of MARC21 governs MARC production
edges.benefit_of_coupling: MARC only when ILS needs it

edges.why_related: selection of EAD governs archival finding aids
selected schemas define crosswalk source/target set
edges.example: crosswalk to a schema never adopted

edges.why_related: RDA recording rules are grounded in the LRM entity model
BIBFRAME entities derive from the conceptual model
RDA content values change what is recorded in MARC fields
edges.resolution_rule: apply RDA policy before MARC encoding

edges.why_related: RDA content values populate BIBFRAME entities
MODS supplies the descriptive payload embedded in METS dmdSec
PREMIS supplies preservation metadata in METS amdSec
identifier policy constrains how objects in METS are referenced and resolved
edges.resolution_rule: bind persistent IDs into the package references

edges.why_related: the profile constrains how DC elements may be used
edges.example: optional element used against profile cardinality

edges.why_related: the profile constrains MODS element usage and obligation
vocabularies provide the value constraints referenced by the profile
vocabulary URIs supply the objects/predicates used in RDF
persistent identifiers provide stable URIs for RDF subjects
edges.resolution_rule: mint persistent IDs before RDF subjects

edges.why_related: the profile defines which elements/shapes become RDF
BIBFRAME entities require stable URIs from the identifier system
DC is a common crosswalk target requiring its semantics fixed first
edges.resolution_rule: fix DC usage before mapping to it

edges.why_related: MARC as crosswalk source needs field usage fixed
crosswalks transform rich records into harvestable formats
oai_dc is the baseline format harvesters require
identifiers constrain how harvested records are deduplicated and linked
edges.example: same object harvested under two ids

edges.why_related: conformance is measured against the application profile
remediation targets the defects quality assessment finds
edges.example: editing fields that were already fine

edges.why_related: remediation triggers re-assessment to confirm improvement
edges.example: batch edit assumed correct without re-check
edges.resolution_rule: stop when re-measurement meets target or after max 3 cycles

edges.why_related: vocabularies supply correct values for enrichment/normalization
quality reports inform governance policy and review cadence
profiles are the artifacts governance versions and maintains
simplicity/interoperability of DC competes with descriptive richness of MODS
edges.example: using DC where MODS richness is needed
edges.resolution_rule: choose by required granularity; a profile may layer DC over MODS-derived data

edges.why_related: legacy MARC record model competes with linked-data BIBFRAME model
edges.example: big-bang MARC drop before tooling matures
edges.resolution_rule: run dual-stack; convert incrementally with round-trip validation

edges.why_related: document-centric METS packaging competes with graph-centric RDF expression
edges.example: maintaining METS and RDF that disagree
edges.resolution_rule: derive one from the other; designate the authoritative source

edges.why_related: quality gating competes with aggregation throughput and coverage
edges.risk_of_conflict: low-quality records aggregated or coverage starved
edges.example: exposing unvetted records to a portal
edges.resolution_rule: gate on minimum conformance; quarantine sub-threshold records

edges.why_related: governance stability competes with adopting newly-needed schemas
edges.example: blocking an urgent schema need on process
edges.resolution_rule: governance change-control approves selection changes with impact analysis

conflict_axes.trigger: choosing a flat interoperable schema that drops needed descriptive detail
resolution_order: pick schema meeting granularity then add a profile
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: required granularity dominates: never drop a mandated element for simplicity
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if no single schema meets both interoperability and granularity
conflict_axes.example: DC chosen for items needing MODS-level detail

conflict_axes.trigger: migrating from record-based MARC to entity-based linked data
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: data preservation dominates: no big-bang migration that loses relationships
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if conversion drops relationships beyond tolerance
conflict_axes.example: MARC dropped before BIBFRAME tooling is ready

conflict_axes.trigger: maintaining both a document wrapper and a graph for the same object
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: single source of truth dominates: one representation is authoritative
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if the two representations diverge in content
conflict_axes.example: METS dmdSec and RDF graph disagree on a field

conflict_axes.trigger: gating records on quality reduces aggregated coverage
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: minimum fitness-for-use dominates: never aggregate below conformance floor
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if coverage falls below mandate at the chosen threshold
conflict_axes.example: portal aggregates records missing required dates

conflict_axes.trigger: local refinements diverge from the referenced standard
resolution_order: map local terms to standard terms
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: interoperability dominates: local terms must map back to standard terms
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if local profile breaks exchange with partners
conflict_axes.example: local element with no standard equivalent breaks harvest

conflict_axes.trigger: batch automated edits risk introducing wider errors
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: correctness dominates: irreversible batch edits require human review and an audit trail
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if a batch edit is irreversible or touches high-risk fields
conflict_axes.example: mass normalization corrupting valid edge-case values

conflict_axes.trigger: recording every preservation event grows metadata without bound
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: auditability dominates for risk events; routine events may be summarized under policy
conflict_axes.example: every periodic fixity check stored as a full event

conflict_axes.trigger: prioritizing discovery fields while under-capturing preservation metadata
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: function-map coverage dominates: no function may be silently dropped
conflict_axes.example: rich discovery records with no checksums

conflict_axes.trigger: deciding which WEMI entities receive their own persistent identifiers
resolution_order: assign PIDs at those levels only
conflict_axes.dominance_logic: citability dominates: assign PIDs at every level that must be independently cited
conflict_axes.escalation_threshold: if PID strategy mismatches entity model
conflict_axes.example: minting item PIDs but none for Works needed for linking

edge_cases.trigger: crosswalk from a rich schema to flat DC
edge_cases.failure_mode: semantic loss from collapsing distinct elements
edge_cases.example: MARC relator-coded contributors collapse to one dc:contributor
edge_cases.detection_method: round-trip test comparing source elements to recovered elements
resolution: record mapping notes for lossy fields
retain richer record as authoritative source

edge_cases.example: mapping a note field onto a description field
edge_cases.detection_method: expert spot-check of high-frequency mappings against element definitions
resolution: require human confirmation for semantic equivalence

edge_cases.trigger: structMap references files or sections not present
edge_cases.example: structMap points to a fileSec entry that was removed
edge_cases.detection_method: validate every structMap fptr/ID against fileSec and dmdSec/amdSec IDs

edge_cases.trigger: preserved object ingested without a fixity value
edge_cases.example: object stored with no checksum or message digest
edge_cases.detection_method: scan PREMIS objects for missing fixity/messageDigest
resolution: compute and record fixity at ingest

edge_cases.trigger: a published identifier is reassigned or reused
edge_cases.example: a DOI minted for the wrong manifestation reused for another
edge_cases.detection_method: diff identifier-to-target bindings against published history
resolution: mint a new PID and tombstone the erroneous one

edge_cases.failure_mode: stale URIs/headings break linking and collocation
edge_cases.example: a deprecated LCSH URI still used across records
edge_cases.detection_method: periodic reconciliation of stored URIs against current vocabulary

edge_cases.trigger: profile diverges from referenced namespace revision
edge_cases.failure_mode: records validate locally but break exchange
edge_cases.example: local refinement not aligned with updated DCMI Terms
edge_cases.detection_method: compare profile element URIs against current namespace definitions

edge_cases.failure_mode: relationships dropped or duplicate Works created
edge_cases.example: complex linking fields not surviving conversion
edge_cases.detection_method: compare entity/relationship counts pre/post conversion against expected

edge_cases.trigger: incremental harvest misses updates or deletes
edge_cases.failure_mode: aggregated set drifts out of sync with source
edge_cases.example: deleted records still present in the portal
edge_cases.detection_method: compare datestamps and deleted-record handling against source counts
resolution: fix datestamp/deletion support at the endpoint

edge_cases.example: a regex normalization corrupting valid edge-case dates
edge_cases.detection_method: re-run quality assessment on the edited set and compare deltas
resolution: fix rule and re-run on a test set first

edge_cases.trigger: a metric value labeled observed without observed data
edge_cases.example: a heuristic conformance estimate labeled observed
edge_cases.detection_method: scan value_labels for observed/experimentally_validated with no source eligibility

workflow.objective: fix metadata function scope and entity model before any encoding choice
acceptance_tests: every required function mapped
WEMI levels distinguishable in samples
workflow.do_first_because: function scope and entity model are the highest-coupling foundations all later steps depend on

workflow.objective: select fitting schema(s) for each resource class and function
acceptance_tests: each required element supported by a selected schema
schemas recognized by exchange partners
workflow.do_first_because: schema choice constrains every encoding, crosswalk, and harvest step downstream

workflow.objective: establish vocabularies, ownership, and versioning policy
acceptance_tests: every active artifact has an owner and version
vocabularies resolve to current authorities
workflow.do_first_because: governance and vocabularies must exist before profiles and content rules lock

workflow.objective: set content/transcription rules and controlled access points
acceptance_tests: values conform to RDA element definitions
access points reconciled to authorities
workflow.do_first_because: content rules must be fixed before records are encoded to avoid inconsistent transcription

workflow.objective: author the application profile with cardinality and value constraints
acceptance_tests: every profile element resolves to a namespace term
constraints expressible as shapes
workflow.do_first_because: the profile makes interoperability concrete and is the reference for quality and RDF

workflow.objective: create descriptive records in the selected schemas per profile
acceptance_tests: records validate against schema
records conform to profile cardinality
workflow.do_first_because: descriptive records depend on selection, content rules, and the profile being fixed

workflow.objective: capture preservation metadata and mint persistent identifiers
acceptance_tests: every object has fixity and a provenance event
every published PID resolves correctly
workflow.do_first_because: PIDs and fixity are high-irreversibility; establish them before packaging and publishing

workflow.objective: package complex objects and/or express metadata as linked data
acceptance_tests: METS validates with all referenced files present
RDF parses and uses resolvable URIs
workflow.do_first_because: structural packaging and linked-data expression consume descriptive, preservation, and identifier outputs

workflow.objective: author crosswalks and expose/aggregate records for harvesting
acceptance_tests: round-trip preserves mandatory elements
harvest returns complete valid records
workflow.do_first_because: crosswalks and harvesting depend on stable schema usage and validated records

workflow.objective: measure quality, remediate defects, and apply change-controlled locks
acceptance_tests: targeted quality dimensions meet thresholds
remediation re-measured and audited
workflow.do_first_because: quality gating and human review must pass before any artifact is hard-locked

dominance_rules.trigger: a metadata change is faster but risks correctness or interoperability
dominance_rules.rule: never accept a speed win that fails validation or breaks exchange
dominance_rules.required_action: block lock until QUALITY_ASSESS and schema validation pass
dominance_rules.example: a batch shortcut rejected because it broke profile conformance

dominance_rules.trigger: a high-value node lacks its prerequisite
dominance_rules.rule: respect dependency precedence over raw importance
dominance_rules.required_action: place prerequisite (e.g., META_TYPE_MODEL) before dependents in priority_order
dominance_rules.example: schema selection deferred until the function map exists

dominance_rules.trigger: a precise number lacks eligible evidence
dominance_rules.rule: label honestly as heuristic rather than overclaim observed
dominance_rules.required_action: keep observed_impact/data_quality at 0.0 with heuristic labels
dominance_rules.example: a conformance estimate kept heuristic, not labeled observed

dominance_rules.trigger: records or profiles are about to be locked before quality checks
dominance_rules.rule: QA must pass before soft/hard lock
dominance_rules.required_action: require QUALITY_ASSESS thresholds before lock_condition advances
dominance_rules.example: a profile lock blocked until conformance is measured

dominance_rules.trigger: an irreversible action (PID publish, batch remediation, hard lock)
dominance_rules.rule: human review dominates for irreversible or high-risk actions
dominance_rules.required_action: set human_review_required and capture a decision record
dominance_rules.example: PID publication held for review before minting

dominance_rules.rule: stabilize schema and profile before mass record creation
dominance_rules.required_action: freeze profile (soft_lock) before descriptive encoding scales
dominance_rules.example: halt bulk authoring until the profile is approved

dominance_rules.trigger: a claim exceeds what the source registry supports
dominance_rules.rule: every estimate must reference an eligible source
dominance_rules.required_action: attach SRC_HEURISTIC_PRIOR to all heuristic estimates
dominance_rules.example: an interoperability claim downgraded to heuristic

dominance_rules.trigger: a local refinement breaks exchange with partners
dominance_rules.rule: interoperability dominates; local terms must map to standard terms
dominance_rules.required_action: map local profile elements back to standard namespace terms
dominance_rules.example: a local element with no standard equivalent removed or mapped

dominance_rules.trigger: one metadata function is dropped to optimize another
dominance_rules.rule: no required function may be silently dropped
dominance_rules.required_action: verify every in-scope function still mapped before lock
dominance_rules.example: preservation metadata reinstated after a discovery-only optimization

dominance_rules.trigger: a convenient ordering would create a dependency cycle
dominance_rules.rule: keep dependency edges acyclic; convert weaker links to sequence/feedback
dominance_rules.required_action: convert one direction to a sequence or feedback edge and record the repair
dominance_rules.example: assess<->remediate modeled as dependency plus a bounded feedback edge

anti_rework_rules.rule: resolve metadata function scope before selecting any schema
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a schema chosen on wrong scope forces re-selection and re-encoding
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: schema selected before the function map exists
anti_rework_rules.example: MARC chosen, then preservation function added

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix the entity model before content/transcription rules
anti_rework_rules.rationale: content rules built on an unclear model cause inconsistent records
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: RDA applied with ambiguous WEMI identity
anti_rework_rules.example: Work identity decided after cataloging began

anti_rework_rules.rule: bind controlled vocabularies before finalizing the profile
anti_rework_rules.rationale: a profile without value vocabularies cannot constrain values
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: profile element with no value source

anti_rework_rules.rule: finalize the profile before mass descriptive encoding
anti_rework_rules.rationale: records authored before the profile must be re-edited to conform
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: bulk records created then cardinality changed
anti_rework_rules.example: thousands of records re-edited after a profile fix

anti_rework_rules.rule: mint persistent identifiers before linked-data subjects
anti_rework_rules.rationale: triples on ephemeral URIs break on migration
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: RDF subject is a local non-persistent URL

anti_rework_rules.rule: validate descriptive and preservation payloads before METS packaging
anti_rework_rules.rationale: packaging invalid payloads propagates errors into the wrapper
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: METS built referencing an invalid dmdSec
anti_rework_rules.example: whole package re-built after a dmdSec fix

anti_rework_rules.rule: fix schema usage before authoring crosswalks
anti_rework_rules.rationale: mapping to a moving target forces crosswalk rewrites
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: crosswalk authored against a changing profile
anti_rework_rules.example: crosswalk redone after MODS profile change

anti_rework_rules.rationale: blind remediation edits correct fields and misses real defects
anti_rework_rules.violation_signal: batch edits with no prior assessment
anti_rework_rules.example: fields edited that were already conformant

anti_rework_rules.rule: pass human review and QA before any hard lock
anti_rework_rules.rationale: hard-locking before review forces version increments to undo
anti_rework_rules.example: a profile hard-locked then reopened for a defect

iteration_protocol.trigger: validator or quality report flags a failure
iteration_protocol.detection: compare validation_report and quality deltas to thresholds
acceptance_tests: every failure mapped to a subsystem

iteration_protocol.detection: rank defects by risk_score and downstream coupling
acceptance_tests: high-risk defects ranked first
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: queue empty or only sub-threshold defects remain

iteration_protocol.trigger: a defect touches a locked or high-coupling node
iteration_protocol.detection: trace dependents via edges and node.dependencies
acceptance_tests: all dependents of the changed node identified
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: impact set stable across a pass

iteration_protocol.trigger: a prioritized defect is ready to fix
iteration_protocol.detection: map defect type to repair_routing subsystem
acceptance_tests: repair owner recorded
fix applied

iteration_protocol.detection: re-run kb_validator and targeted quality checks
acceptance_tests: previously failing checks now pass
no new failures

iteration_protocol.trigger: new evidence or repeated failures change confidence
acceptance_tests: nodes exceeding delta flagged for revisit
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no node exceeds the posterior delta

iteration_protocol.trigger: an upstream node changes after a dependent was locked
iteration_protocol.detection: detect upstream change against lock state of dependents
acceptance_tests: all affected dependents downgraded and queued
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: no locked dependent has a changed upstream

iteration_protocol.trigger: an irreversible or high-risk decision or unresolved high-risk defect
acceptance_tests: decision record complete with approver
iteration_protocol.stop_condition: human review approves or rejects with record

human_review_required_for: hard lock of any profile or record set

checks.repair_action: scores computed by formula script within tol 0.02

version_increment_rules: increment on any hard-locked artifact change
increment when formulas or metric weights change
lock_downgrade_rules: downgrade dependents when an upstream node changes
downgrade when an evidence label is revised
